question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer now, and what redacted payload plus observer-failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing lifecycle surface, but choosing what install metadata plugins may see and whether observer failures can affect an already-written install is a security and product boundary decision.

options.title: Add Minimal Observer
options.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

options.title: Keep Pre-Install Only
options.body: Declare `security.installPolicy` and `before_install` sufficient for install security, then narrow or close the audit-observer request separately.

options.title: Defer To ClawHub Trust Design
options.body: Hold the observer until maintainers define a broader ClawHub trust/provenance API that can supply the same audit events.

recommendation.title: Add Minimal Observer
recommendation.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata plus documented fail-open logging semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses ClawHub skill install behavior and public plugin lifecycle API shape, and steipete is the strongest product-routing signal from discussion and adjacent history.
